leverage.exposure: No leverage is open right now — the balance is positive and the squad is legal, so there is no unwind deadline outstanding today. But the recommended structure opens one deliberately, and its margin is zero rather than merely thin. The bid was set equal to cash plus the designated unwind's market value, to the euro, so winning the auction leaves the balance negative until that sale is executed, and the sale clears it to precisely nothing. The bid is fixed once placed; the unwind is not, because market values are re-priced every evening. If the designated unwind's value falls at tonight's tick, the sale no longer covers the purchase and the balance rides negative into the matchday lock, which scores zero for the entire matchday. That is the risk that outranks everything else here, and it is checkable: the first run after tonight's tick must re-read the value rather than reuse the stored one, and either re-place the bid against the new figure or switch the unwind to the next defender up, accepting the points cost. There is slack — roughly a day between the tick and the auction resolving — so this is a scheduled check, not an emergency, provided the check actually happens.

binding_gap: The binding constraint is not a position and not the budget — it is the unwind. The squad is legal in one shape only, so the fielded eleven cannot be improved except by replacing its weakest member, and the weakest member that can actually be sold is not the same as the weakest member on the pitch. That single fact decides every buy on the board this run: the live bid is the only purchase whose funding leg is also the man it displaces. Defence is where the depth is thinnest in quality terms, and the live bid addresses exactly that slot.

verdict.detail: No new action. Hold the Pinckert bid exactly as placed and change nothing else. The board threw up its best asset of the season since the last run — Alphonso Davies, freshly listed by Kickbase at market value — and he still loses to Pinckert, not on merit but on structure: with the squad at eleven, one buy permits exactly one sale, and every unwind large enough to fund Davies is a better player than the one Pinckert displaces. Pinckert's route is the only one that removes the weakest fielded body. Higher scoring average does not beat a better unwind. The one thing that genuinely needs watching is not on the board at all: the Pinckert bid was sized to the euro against Lokonga's market value, so it has no headroom, and tonight's value tick can turn a safe unwind into a negative balance at the matchday lock.
